newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Strike ballot at Lebowa over wages.
newsitem.headline: Strike ballot at Lebowa over wages.

text.p: Annual wage talks at Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd have deadlocked and the union has proceeded with a strike ballot, managers Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd said on Friday.
Amplats said in a statement negotiations had stalled at a conciliation board and if Lebowa workers voted in favour of strike action, a strike could begin on Sunday evening.
"The management of Amplats regrets to announce that the wage negotiations at Lebowa Platinum Mines have deadlocked at Conciliation Board," it said.
"The company is doing everything in its power to prevent strike action," Amplats added.
The company is offering a seven percent wage increase against the National Union of Mineworkers' (NUM) demand for 15 percent.
The NUM is also demanding parity with historically better-paid white workers in terms of standby allowance, retirement fund, annual leave and medical aid benefits.
On August 26 the NUM declared a dispute and the matter was taken to a conciliation board.
